data.name: Ariadne
data.long_meaning: Daughter of King Minos of Crete, Ariadne was a beloved and loyal companion to Theseus. She provided him with a thread to find his way out of the labyrinth and gave him a ball of thread so he could retrace his steps back to the entrance.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of loyalty and devotion in challenging circumstances

in_hebrew.name: אריאדנה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אריאדנה מורכב משתי מילים: אריה ודנה, שפירושם קורבן מרצון ונדבה של קודש. השם נגזר מהשפה היוונית ומשמש ככינוי לנשים בישראל ובקהילות יהודיות אחרות. מבחינה היסטורית, השם אריאדנה שימש ככינוי לאישה שהייתה קורבן מרצון לאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Αριάδνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αριάδνη προέρχεται από την αρχαία ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'πολύ σεβαστή, αγία, και δίκαιη'. Στην ελληνική μυθολογία, η Αριάδνη ήταν κόρη του Μίνωα και της Πασιφάης, και ήταν γνωστή για την πονηρότητά της και την αγάπη της για τον Θεό. Στην Εκκλησία, το όνομα Αριάδνη χρησιμοποιείται ως σύμβολο της πνευματικής αγνότητας και της αρετής.

in_latin.name: Ariadne
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Ariadne originates from ancient Greek and Latin languages, signifying 'very holy, sacred, and righteous'. In Christian tradition, Ariadne represents spiritual purity and virtue. Historically, the name was associated with a figure in Greek mythology, but its adoption in Christian contexts emphasizes its connection to sacred and righteous living.

in_english.name: Ariadne
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ariadne, derived from Greek roots, signifies 'most holy, sacred, and virtuous'. Etymologically, it connects to ancient Greek mythology and Christian tradition, symbolizing spiritual purity and righteousness. Historically, the name Ariadne has been used across various Christian cultures, reflecting its enduring significance in the tradition.

data.cultural_impact: Ariadne is a symbol of loyalty and love, as well as a reminder of the challenges we face in life and the importance of finding our way back to safety, comfort, and civilization. Her name is associated with the ancient Greek myths of Theseus and the labyrinth, and the motif of a narrative thread that guides us through the twists and turns of our personal experiences.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Ariadne could represent the constant presence and guidance of God in our lives. Like the thread she gave to Theseus, her love and support could help us navigate the complex labyrinth of life and enable us to find our way back to the restoration and renewal that can only come from God. Her story can serve as a reminder of the power of love, loyalty, and faith, and the importance of trusting in Divine Providence.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ariadne was a Cretan princess and the wife of Theseus, the legendary Athenian hero. The name Ariadne carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ariadne remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Elizabeth Ariadne in Jerusalem, Israel credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Ariadne, which means "Most Beloved". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Ariadne is the goddess of mazes and labyrinths in Greek mythology, symbolizing the complexities of life and the journey towards enlightenment. In Christianity, she represents the divine guidance and unwavering faith that leads us through life's labyrinth, ultimately leading us to the heart of God.
